title: console: StorageUsageBanner probes the cloud-only GET /api/v1/usage/storage on every shell mount, so every page load logs a 404 on a non-cloud deployment
body:
## Symptom

On a self-hosted or open-source objectstack runtime, every console page load issues `GET /api/v1/usage/storage` and gets `404`. The browser console shows `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404` on every navigation that remounts the shell.

## Mechanism

- `StorageUsageBanner` (objectui#10439, landed as #10910) is rendered unconditionally in `packages/app-shell/src/console/ConsoleShell.tsx`.
- Its hook `useStorageUsageReading` defaults to `enabled = true` and calls `readStorageUsage()`, which fetches `${apiBase}/usage/storage`.
- The endpoint is served only by cloud's `StorageUsageEndpointPlugin`, as objectui#10439 itself records.
- objectstack's own runtime mounts no such route, and `/api/v1/discovery` advertises none. The hook's `.catch` swallows the failure, so the banner correctly renders nothing, but the request is made and fails on every mount.

## Reproduction

1. Boot objectstack's showcase at objectui pin `dd3f7e1be356` (`objectstack dev`).
2. Sign in and open any console page.
3. The network log shows `GET /api/v1/usage/storage → 404`, repeated on each shell mount.

## Expected

The banner only asks when the runtime serves the reading: gate the hook on something the server advertises (discovery or runtime config), the way a capability-gated surface does. A deployment without the endpoint then issues no request. Machine-readable surfaces here should neither lie nor be guessed at.
